transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
I don’t enjoy my classes or my art anymore, and the things that used to excite me just feel flat and pointless. I just feel completely drained and disconnected from everything lately.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did it start after a specific stressful event or life change?

These feelings have been going on pretty steadily for about eight months now. It started after I was passed over for a tenure-track promotion I had worked really hard for, which happened right around the same time my teaching load and work pressure increased.
Have you had any periods of at least two months during these eight months when you felt back to your usual self, or has it been present most of the time without much relief?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt back to my usual self at all. It has been completely constant and heavy every single day since I missed out on the promotion. There really hasn't been any break or relief from it.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months in the past when your mood and interest in things were back to normal, or has this low mood been present most of the time for years?

Before I was passed over for the promotion eight months ago, my mood and interest in things were completely normal, and I had never felt this way before. Since then, though, these feelings have been completely constant without any periods of relief or return to how I used to be.
Have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness during this time?

Yes, my sleep has been awful—I either lie awake for hours replaying work emails or wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with a heavy anxiety and can't fall back asleep. I've also been overwhelmed by feelings of worthlessness, constantly telling myself I'm a fraud and a disappointment to my husband and colleagues since I missed that promotion.
Did these symptoms begin within about 3 months of the promotion setback and work stress, or did they start later and feel out of proportion to that stressor?

Yes, they started pretty much immediately after I was passed over for the promotion. The changes in my mood and sleep began steadily right after that setback, so it was definitely within that three-month window.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or any thoughts of hurting yourself?

On my worst days, especially after a long, unproductive evening at my desk, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up or could quietly slip away. But these are just passive thoughts, and I don't have any plan or intention to actually act on them.

Since this started after the promotion setback, have you felt the distress is mainly tied to that stressor and your work situation, or does it feel like a depression that is out of proportion and affecting most areas of your life even when you are not thinking about work?

It definitely feels like a heavy, constant depression that has spread far beyond my work. Even when I'm not thinking about my job, it affects almost every area of my life, like my passion for art and my marriage, where my husband has had to take over most of the household chores. It just feels like a gray film is over everything now, regardless of where I am.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks during this time when you felt mostly back to normal, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day without relief?

No, I haven't had even a two-week break where I felt back to normal. These feelings of sadness and loss of interest have been constant nearly every single day for the past eight months. There hasn't been any period where I felt like my old self.
Have you ever had a period of at least a few days where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or were more impulsive than normal?
No, I have never experienced periods of feeling unusually energized, euphoric, or needing less sleep. My energy has generally been normal in the past, and lately, it has been quite low.

Have these symptoms caused a clear decline in your ability to function at work, at home, or socially, beyond what you would expect from the promotion setback alone? Also, do you feel sad or empty most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, it has caused a major decline—I’ve fallen behind on grading, started avoiding department events and canceling student art activities, and my husband has had to take over most of the chores at home. I also feel a heavy, hollow sadness like a gray film over everything most days, and it doesn't lift even when something objectively good happens.

Did your symptoms begin within 3 months of the promotion setback, and do they feel mainly tied to that stressor—or do they seem more like a depression that affects most areas of your life even when you are not thinking about work?

Yes, they started pretty much immediately after the promotion setback eight months ago. While that was definitely the trigger, the depression has now spread to affect almost every part of my life, like my marriage, my art, and my daily mood, rather than just being about my job.

Have your symptoms felt mainly tied to the promotion setback and work stress, or have they persisted as a broader depression affecting most areas of your life even when you are not thinking about work?

It definitely feels like a broader depression that has spread to almost every area of my life. Even when I am at home away from work, trying to paint or spending time with my husband, that heavy, flat sadness is always there and just won't lift. It is no longer just about the job setback anymore.

Before the promotion setback, did you ever have a similar episode of depression or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks? Also, have the symptoms been out of proportion to the stressor and continued even after any improvement in the work situation?

No, I have never experienced an episode of depression or lost interest in things like this before the promotion setback. As for my work situation, it hasn't really improved, so it's hard to say, but these feelings definitely feel far out of proportion to just a job setback now.

Have you experienced any other major stressful or traumatic event around the time this started, such as a serious loss, accident, or threat to your safety? And if the work setback were to improve, do you think your symptoms would quickly improve too, or would they likely keep going?

No, there weren't any other traumatic events or threats to my safety—the promotion setback was the main thing. And because this heavy sadness is so constant and doesn't lift even when good things happen, I feel like the symptoms would probably keep going even if my work situation got better.

Since the promotion setback, have your symptoms felt mainly tied to that stressor, or have they continued even when you are not thinking about work and started to feel like a broader depression? Also, have they lasted most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, they have definitely turned into a broader depression that stays with me even when I'm completely away from work, like a heavy, hollow sadness and a gray film over everything. These feelings have been present pretty steadily, most of the day nearly every day, for the entire eight months since the promotion setback.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood: symptoms began within 3 months of an identifiable psychosocial stressor (failure to obtain promotion plus increased work pressure), are persistent and distressing, and cause clear functional impairment. Depressive symptoms are present (anhedonia, low mood, worthlessness, sleep disturbance, passive death wishes), but the interview repeatedly emphasizes a stressor-linked onset rather than a standalone major depressive episode; there is no evidence of mania or psychosis. Major depressive episode (F32) remains a key differential, but the stressor-temporal relationship and adjustment-pattern framing support F43.23 best.
